draft.title: The reactivity series of metals
card: The reactivity series ranks metals by how easily they lose electrons to form positive ions. The metal at the top loses electrons most easily, so it is the most reactive.
A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from a solution of its ions. The more reactive metal goes into solution as ions and the less reactive metal forms as a solid.
Example: zinc placed in copper(II) sulfate solution becomes coated in copper, because zinc is more reactive than copper. Copper placed in zinc sulfate solution shows no change.
Metals in order from most to least reactive include magnesium, zinc, iron, tin, lead, copper and silver.
draft.remember: The more easily a metal loses electrons, the higher it sits in the reactivity series, and it displaces metals below it.

a.q: What puts a metal near the top of the reactivity series?
opts: It has a very high density
It is very hard to cut
a.why: The series ranks metals by how easily they lose electrons, so a metal near the top loses them most easily. Metals form positive ions by losing electrons, not gaining them. Density and hardness are physical properties and do not set the order.
a.clue: Think about what the reactivity series ranks metals by.

b.q: Mia places a strip of magnesium in one beaker of iron(II) sulfate solution and a strip of copper in another. What does she see?
opts: Iron forms on the magnesium only
Iron forms on the copper strip only
Iron forms on both of the strips
Iron forms on neither of the strips
b.why: Magnesium is more reactive than iron, so it displaces iron from solution and iron forms as a solid. Copper is less reactive than iron, so it cannot displace iron and nothing happens.
b.clue: Only a metal above iron in the reactivity series can displace iron.

b.best: Iron forms on the magnesium only
